<!-- pr-reviewer: 7d8a125a537ed3188237c2381091cc391c947263 -->

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Built on the self-hosted runner (quick gate on the merged tree, main 6711cd3b): run 43520308888 succeeded. post, sim, motion, app and ui suites 0 failed (16.1 min); clippy -D warnings on camcraft-app, camcraft-motion and camcraft-sim clean. The Windows-only reading does not apply (no cfg(windows) lines). I read the new tests but did not separately run them against old code; the PR body reports a mutation check for the Sodick refusal.

## What looks good

- Rough-only programs are unchanged. No existing golden changed; the only golden is the new `wire_contour_punch_skims.nc`. `wire-iso.cps` skim logic only runs when an `EdmCondition` arrives while the wire is already threaded (`skimPending`). A tab cut-off is its own section, with threaded reset in `onSection`, so it is not read as a skim.
- Per-pass program in the new golden: rough C110 at X-20.165, skim 1 S21 at X-20.145, skim 2 S31 reversed at X-20.135. Each skim returns to the threading point, then writes `(SKIM n)`, the condition select and `FX-COMP-OFF` again before its first move. Compensation stays off because the offset is in the path. Wire stays threaded. One thread and one cut.
- `sodick-wire.cps`: the change is confined to `onParameter(EdmCondition)`. The PR #1506 fixes (G40 on every positioning and threading move, `C###` header note) are untouched in the diff. A condition change after the section's first cut is refused by name, so no skim is cut on the rough C word. The PR body reports a mutation check.
- Verify (`crates/sim/src/verify/wire/`): `passes.rs` splits the path at each return to the threading point and judges each move at its own pass's kerf. Direction of change:
  - Gouge check, per move: moves from the rough kerf to the move's own pass kerf. This is tighter for no pass and looser only for a skim, whose real kerf is smaller. The decision record shows the old reading was a false 0.0200 mm gouge, and a test pins that a skim 0.05 mm too near is still a 0.05 mm gouge.
  - Threading clearance: now the widest pass's kerf, which is not looser than before.
  - Slug law: each pass is swept at its own offset and the results are joined.
  - A path that does not return once per pass is `Unreadable`, a refusal. Skims on an open run, or with tabs, are refused in the law, at the door and in the post.
  - I found no check that is loosened without proof.
- Punch slug: skims do not bypass the existing hold law. An untabbed freed piece must be captured (`job.capture`), otherwise an `Unsupported` finding blocks the post. Tabs plus skims are refused by name. So a skim after a dropped slug is a refusal, not silent. The decision record states it.
- Validation at the door (`condition_of` / `check_passes`): empty or unstated condition, another wire diameter, a pass nearer than the finish, a skim farther out than its predecessor, and skims with a taper, burnout, tabs or 4-axis cut. `is_sane` bounds `SKIMS_MAX` = 16 and condition ids.
- Project file: `skims` is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = empty)]`, so old files open and rough-only files write unchanged. Stamp writes nothing for no skims. Edits go through `EditOperationParams` (undoable) and the MCP params door.
- No unwrap/expect/panic outside tests. No snapshot PNG changes. `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #538` are present. `docs/decisions/538-wire-skims.md` is present. No `cfg(windows)` or per-OS change. The body states the output was not run on a real EDM control (D10).

## Results merged with main

Run: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43520308888 (success, see above).

## Requested before merge

None from the read.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- The `wire-iso.cps` header comment line now runs past the wrapped width (cosmetic).
- `announce_skims` closes a pass at any non-rapid move ending at the threading XY. A path that passes through the threading point mid-pass would be counted as a pass end, but then the pass count check refuses it, so it fails safe.
- The UI skim editor is follow-up #1148.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
